scope: Finite ideal-Boolean/event model; digital artificial-load concept only

assumptions.timer_pulse_model: Instantaneous positive non-retriggerable pulse; no gate or timer propagation model
assumptions.coincidence_exclusion_status: Declared diagnostic assumption, not a certified physical aperture

scenarios.title: Startup is inhibited without assuming DFF power-on state

checks.assertion: reset-low sets block and holds RUN low
timeout is explicitly unknown until safe rearm

scenarios.title: Held request through readiness return cannot gain admission

checks.assertion: readiness did not create another trigger
held request cannot clear block or RUN
held invalid request eventually records timeout

scenarios.title: Qualified positive and negative phases end normally without false timeout

checks.assertion: safe rearm resolves latches and captures positive direction
positive bridge admitted
normal completion consumes admission immediately
later timer expiry does not falsely record timeout
next rearm captures negative direction
second normal phase also avoids false timeout

notes: The example includes a 100us all-off gap and explicit rearm after the first timer expires; physical current quiescence is an input assumption.

scenarios.title: Early request drop consumes admission without an automatic balancing phase

checks.assertion: 50us phase stops and remains consumed
no timeout or automatic new trigger follows

scenarios.title: Request low-high within one timer interval cannot reopen output

checks.assertion: busy trigger is ignored without timer extension
consumed block prevents reopened RUN
ended repeated request does not create a false timeout

scenarios.title: New timer after expiry has no authority without explicit rearm

checks.assertion: raw request can start an internal second timer
second timer does not restore consumed admission

scenarios.title: Stuck request is cut off by timer and sticky timeout

checks.assertion: timer directly removes RUN at nominal expiry
later request edge cannot clear sticky timeout
later timer ending with request low preserves timeout
only explicit safe rearm clears the timeout
fresh request after rearm can be admitted

scenarios.title: Request/timer coincidence leaves timeout classification unqualified

checks.assertion: timer gate still commands RUN low
classification is unknown rather than favourable

notes: This is a rejected classification trace; Boolean event ordering cannot resolve the actual setup/hold/metastability event.

scenarios.title: Each permission drop consumes admission and recovery cannot resume

checks.assertion: mon_permit loss sets block and stops RUN
mon_permit recovery cannot reopen RUN
ext_sup_ok loss sets block and stops RUN
ext_sup_ok recovery cannot reopen RUN
route_locked loss sets block and stops RUN
route_locked recovery cannot reopen RUN
reset_ready loss sets block and stops RUN
reset_ready recovery cannot reopen RUN
rails_qualified loss sets block and stops RUN
rails_qualified recovery cannot reopen RUN

scenarios.title: Both-high and both-low phase bits inhibit and consume admission

checks.assertion: invalid (True, True) drops BASE_GOOD and RUN
restored bits after (True, True) do not resume
invalid (False, False) drops BASE_GOOD and RUN
restored bits after (False, False) do not resume

scenarios.title: Valid live raw direction swap cannot reverse captured diagonal

checks.assertion: captured positive direction remains active
XOR does not diagnose a valid simultaneous swap

notes: The raw swap violates the held-input contract; captured-direction stability is demonstrated, complete command-consistency protection is not.

scenarios.title: Unsafe rearm never clears state; explicit qualified rearm does

checks.assertion: request prevents latch clearance
timer prevents latch clearance
quiescence prevents latch clearance
monitor prevents latch clearance
supervision prevents latch clearance
invalid_direction prevents latch clearance
qualified explicit rearm clears unknown timeout and block
driver rearm does not modify the monitor input

scenarios.title: Two sources retain independent timer and rearm ownership

checks.assertion: source0 fault does not interrupt independently permitted source1
source1 rearm cannot clear source0 consumed block

scenarios.title: Brownout leaves model unqualified until external reset and rearm

checks.assertion: qualified warning first inhibits output
out-of-range state is unknown, not falsely safe
recovery begins blocked with unknown timeout
readiness alone does not rearm
explicit safe rearm resolves control state

notes: Timer/output/DFF behaviour during invalid supply is not simulated as valid hardware logic. External reset and timer-startup qualification are assumed on recovery.

scenarios.title: Timer failure witness remains unprotected without external interruption

checks.assertion: stuck-high timer has no falling edge and no sticky timeout
driver alone permits a 500us held request under this injected fault
external supervisor interruption stops RUN and sets block
supervision recovery cannot resume

notes: UNPROTECTED witness: the native timer plus these latches cannot bound duration if timer OUT itself fails high and request remains high.

SET-open is an unqualified analogue timer fault, not simulated as a vendor-established stuck-high transfer function. This injected stuck-high witness demonstrates why a reliable timeout is not credited for SET-open.
An external watchdog is represented only by EXT_SUP_OK dropping; no watchdog circuit is implemented or validated by this study.
Conditional bookkeeping: 3mA for 500us would be 1500nC; current regulation and actual delivered charge are outside this Boolean model.
